The `mrmhub` package exposes more than two hundred functions across import, processing, plotting,
and reporting. A typical end-to-end workflow uses fewer than fifteen of them, in roughly this
order. Use this page as a quick reminder of which function does what; click any function name for
the full reference.

## Workflow order

| Stage | Function | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Import | [`import_data_mrmhub()`](../reference/import_data_mrmhub.html) / [`import_data_masshunter()`](../reference/import_data_masshunter.html) / [`import_data_skyline()`](../reference/import_data_skyline.html) | Read integrated peak data |
| Metadata | [`import_metadata_msorganiser()`](../reference/import_metadata_msorganiser.html) / [`add_metadata()`](../reference/add_metadata.html) | Link analysis / feature / ISTD annotation |
| Setup | [`set_analysis_order()`](../reference/set_analysis_order.html) | Set acquisition order |
| Normalisation | [`normalize_by_istd()`](../reference/normalize_by_istd.html) | Per-feature ISTD normalisation |
| Drift correction | [`correct_drift_loess()`](../reference/correct_drift_loess.html) / [`correct_drift_gaussiankernel()`](../reference/correct_drift_gaussiankernel.html) | Smooth run-order drift |
| Batch correction | [`correct_batch_centering()`](../reference/correct_batch_centering.html) | Align medians across batches |
| Quantitation | [`quantify_by_istd()`](../reference/quantify_by_istd.html) / [`quantify_by_calibration()`](../reference/quantify_by_calibration.html) | Concentration values |
| QC metrics | [`calc_qc_metrics()`](../reference/calc_qc_metrics.html) | Per-feature CV, bias, etc. |
| Filtering | [`filter_features_qc()`](../reference/filter_features_qc.html) | Pass/fail features against thresholds |
| Reporting | [`save_report_xlsx()`](../reference/save_report_xlsx.html) / [`save_dataset_csv()`](../reference/save_dataset_csv.html) | Export final dataset |

## Visualisation at each stage

Plotting functions follow the same workflow logic — see
[Visualisation Functions](manual-08-visualization.html) for the grouped reference, or
[The MRMhub Workflow](tutorial-02-basic-workflow.html) for a walked-through example.

## Reading the function names

A naming convention runs through the public API. Once internalised, function names mostly
predict themselves:

- `import_data_*()` — read raw integrated peak data from a given source
- `import_metadata_*()` — read an annotation table from a given source
- `set_*()` — assign a slot on the experiment
- `add_metadata()` — attach annotation
- `normalize_by_*()` — divide one variable by another (e.g. by ISTD)
- `correct_drift_*()` / `correct_batch_*()` — apply a named correction model
- `quantify_by_*()` — compute concentration values via a given strategy
- `calc_*()` — compute per-feature or per-analysis metrics
- `filter_*()` — apply pass/fail thresholds
- `plot_*()` — return a ggplot2 object
- `save_*()` — write to disk
- `get_*()` — read a derived value from the experiment

See [Key Concepts & Glossary](manual-00-key-concepts.html) for the vocabulary
(`MRMhubExperiment`, `analysis_id`, `feature_id`, `qc_type`, `ISTD`, ...).
